acceptance.gate: Phase 5 gate G5 per master-plan v2.1 §9: F_N within 4% (Coreform 1.84-3.74% across levels); sliding F_T RMS <= 4.5%. Maximum pressure is record/comparison only (mesh-sensitive; coarse mesh does not resolve the contact diameter).

boundary_conditions.contact: finite sliding, surface-to-surface enforcement, isotropic penalty Coulomb friction mu = 0.3, elastic-slip fraction 0.005
boundary_conditions.indenter_motion: upper planar face: prescribed vertical displacement -0.125 in over 0 <= t <= 0.1 (held after), then translation +4.25 in in +x over 0.1 <= t <= 1

geometry.indenter: bottom half of hollow sphere cut through center by plane parallel to x-z plane

loads.note: delta(t) = max(1.25*t - 0.025, 0) for 0 <= t <= 0.1 (initial clearance subtracted); delta = 0.1 in thereafter while patch stays on planar top surface. Sliding comparison window 0.15 <= t <= 0.70; later motion near the finite block edge is outside the half-space solution and excluded.

materials.note: Geometrically nonlinear, small-strain linear elasticity; analytical contact pressure far above yield of ordinary steel — a mathematical verification of elastic contact, not a physical indentation experiment.

mesh_sweep.note: predicted Hertz contact diameter ≈ 0.447 in: slightly smaller than h0, so max pressure is the demanding quantity

provenance.reference_doc_sections: §2 Geometry (Table 1), §3 Material (Table 2), §4 Loading & BC, §6 Hertz-Coulomb accepted solution (Table 3), §7 Results (Tables 4-6)

reference_values.relative_RMS_definition: e_RMS = sqrt(sum((q_i - q_i*)^2)) / sqrt(sum((q_i*)^2)) over output frames in 0.15 <= t <= 0.70

title: Elastic spherical indenter sliding on block (Hertz-Coulomb contact)
